name: Prize crossword No 23,897
preamble: Solve the clues and fit them into the grid wherever they will go jigsaw-wise. You will need to disregard the numbers on the electronic version of the grid.

clue.text: Mystery ingredient in the noise Jaques and I make

indicators.note: to make something is to fashion it out of raw material, so the letters are reworked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written: the melancholy lord in As You Like It
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Jaques and the speaker together produce some indefinable sound, the secret ingredient of their act.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques is the melancholy lord in Shakespeare's As You Like It; a French-sounding name suits a French phrase, which disguises that three of the words are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally 'I don't know what', names an elusive quality that cannot be pinned down, the mystery element in something.

clue.text: Is proud about title backed by lawyers

indicators.note: something backed is moved back to front, so it reads from right to left
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: proud in the sense of sticking out, so 'is proud' means projects
the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Someone stands vain about the honour awarded, with lawyers backing the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proud' here is the builder's sense of standing out from a surface, not pride; JUTS goes round the turned title.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurists are experts in law, a slightly formal synonym for legal practitioners and scholars.

clue.text: Aquatic plant on railway cutting not feeling love

indicators.note: a cutting slices into something, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago
numb means without sensation
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A water plant grows beside a railway cutting, somehow joyless and loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway cutting' reads as a single landscape feature; split it, and the railway cuts into the numbness. EL is the American elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the lotus, a large flowering plant rooted in ponds and shallow water.

clue.text: Punishment arranged by international body may result in finger-licking

definitions.note: a description of the answer's effect rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a chosen order, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: a beating, as in 'give someone stick'
taken as written
the United Nations

explanation.surface: Sanctions imposed by the United Nations might leave a regime licking its fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like diplomacy; the definition is a playful description of eating something glazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky bun is a sweet glazed roll whose sugary coating leaves syrup on the eater's hands.

clue.text: Loch's hero makes precision instruments

definitions.note: describes what the answer is used for; it is a material, not a maker

indicators.note: the possessive asks for the part of the name that belongs after this word, so that word itself is dropped

blocks.note: young Lochinvar is the dashing hero of a ballad in Walter Scott's Marmion

explanation.surface: A Scottish hero turns out to be a craftsman of fine scientific instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Scott's hero Lochinvar and remove the LOCH named in the clue; what remains is the alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Invar is a nickel-steel alloy that barely expands with heat, so it is used for clocks, surveying tapes and other exact apparatus.

clue.text: You finish painting one in silk of high degree

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
in places the preceding pieces inside the following one

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
painting is an art
the Roman numeral
a Queen's Counsel, a senior barrister, is called a silk from the gown they wear

explanation.surface: An instruction to complete a painting of someone dressed in luxurious silk of noble rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of high degree' sounds like social rank but is mathematical. A silk is a Queen's Counsel, a senior British barrister, abbreviated QC.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartic equation or curve is of the fourth degree, a higher order than quadratic or cubic.

clue.text: Opening provided in pursuit of gold and diamonds

blocks.note: OR is gold in heraldry
provided that means on condition, as does if
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: An opportunity opens up for someone chasing gold and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like an opportunity in the treasure hunt; 'in pursuit of' means the condition comes after the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or mouth through which something passes, such as a body aperture.

clue.text: Spread efforts to show remaining horses?

blocks.note: a play is a show on stage
in betting, the field is all the runners other than the favourite

explanation.surface: A gambler spreads stakes across every horse still left in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the racing joke: a punter who backs the field bets against the favourite on everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To play the field is an idiom for avoiding commitment to one person or option, dividing attention among many.

clue.text: Hardy's partner (I said) of siren

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the pieces count by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner, followed by the pronoun

explanation.surface: A comic duo's partner speaks of a seductive singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were the film comedy pair; Laurel then the pronoun, run together, gives the siren's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the legendary Rhine maiden whose singing lured boatmen onto the rock, a siren figure.

clue.text: One in place of Pope (nameless) has supplies for journey

indicators.note: without a name means losing the abbreviation for name
in sets one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral
the Pope's seat in Rome

explanation.surface: A papal stand-in carries provisions for a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in place of Pope' reads as a deputy; really the numeral goes into the Vatican after it drops N, the abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Viatica is the plural of viaticum, Latin for travelling money or provisions taken on a journey.

clue.text: Comedy actress arranged the New York release

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a chosen order, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic actress has organised the American release of her film.
explanation.walkthrough: Athene Seyler was a British stage and film actress best known for comic roles across a long career.
explanation.definitionFit: She was celebrated chiefly in comedy, playing eccentric aunts and dowagers on stage and screen.

clue.text: Beast keeps silence and mother takes the veil

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so one piece holds the others inside it

blocks.note: the Tibetan ox
the hushing sound
a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An animal stays quiet while mother enters a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the veil' is the idiom for becoming a nun, but only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is the double face covering worn in public by some Muslim women, a kind of face covering.

clue.text: Like a rodent developing a thirst

indicators.note: something developing changes its form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature grows thirsty like a small scurrying animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as a rodent getting thirsty; the two words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattish means resembling or characteristic of a rat, the commonest rodent of all.

clue.text: Is obliged to break oaths

indicators.note: to break is to smash into bits, which can be put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is compelled to go back on solemn promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break oaths' is the natural phrase for perjury, but break works on the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Has to expresses necessity or compulsion, exactly as being bound or required to do something does.

clue.text: Force bits of rock to be put among rubbish in the cinema

indicators.note: putting something among things sets it in their midst

blocks.note: g is the symbol for gravitational force
scree is loose stones on a mountainside
to bin is to throw away as rubbish

explanation.surface: Debris is pushed into the litter left on a cinema floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubbish is the verb here, to throw out, which gives BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The big screen is a metonym for film shown in cinemas, as opposed to the small screen of television.

clue.text: Form of megastore for fuel

definitions.note: describes the answer's purpose rather than naming it

indicators.note: a form of something is a different shape of it, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge shop is reshaped into a fuel depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a store for fuel is what the answer is, echoing the store in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large tank holding town gas for supply, so it is a storage vessel serving as a reservoir of energy.

clue.text: Second best hand in the Douay Bible

definitions.note: read with 'Second': what the book called Second Kings elsewhere is named in that Bible

blocks.note: first meaning: in poker, a set of four of a kind beaten only by four aces
second meaning: the Catholic Douay Bible counts Samuel as the first two books of Kings, so Second Kings there has a higher number

explanation.walkthrough: The Douay Bible is an English Catholic translation; it numbers the books of Samuel and Kings together as one to four Kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Quads in the top rank lose only to quads of aces, and the Catholic version labels the later historical book by this name.

clue.text: Cancel instruction for meal within meal, removing starter

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits inside the other
the starter of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

blocks.note: the first meal mentioned: tea, an evening meal in Britain
the second meal mentioned: the midday meal

explanation.surface: A diner cancels an order for one course within another, skipping the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter is the restaurant word for a first course, but here it is the first letter of the outer meal. In Britain tea can be an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unteach is to make someone forget or unlearn what was taught, undoing earlier tuition.

clue.text: King's letter to profiteer is excluded

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Ep. abbreviates epistle, a letter
a ticket tout resells at a profit

explanation.surface: A monarch writes to a racketeer who has been shut out.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is a ticket scalper, someone reselling tickets at inflated prices. Ep. is the usual abbreviation for an epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept out is a phrasal verb meaning barred or prevented from entering, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Timeless conveyances at last on three-dimensional graph

definitions.note: a phrase locating the answer rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: without time means dropping the abbreviation for time

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
cabs convey passengers

explanation.surface: Vehicles that never stop running at last appear plotted on a 3D chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as finally; split it, and last is the final letter of the alphabet, placed before the cabs once T for time is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: In three-dimensional coordinates the third axis, perpendicular to x and y, gives depth or height.

clue.text: Painter not working when clown's about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: off duty
a zany is a clown or buffoon

explanation.surface: An artist downs tools while a clown hangs around.
explanation.walkthrough: Zany is the old noun for a comic assistant or buffoon, not just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Zoffany was a German-born eighteenth-century artist who worked in England, known for conversation pieces.

clue.text: Mark almost anything yellow

definitions.note: used as a noun: a yellow colouring matter

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so a final letter is cut, here from each of two words

blocks.note: a cross, as in X marks the spot
read as two words, any and thing, each losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone will mark nearly anything with a yellow highlighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word into its two halves before clipping: each loses its tail, rather than the whole word losing one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthin is the yellow pigment found in flowers and plants, from the Greek for yellow.

clue.text: What city people talk about in the tube?

definitions.note: a phrase describing where it happens rather than an adjective

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
what people talk about is a topic, a subject of conversation

explanation.surface: Londoners chatting about something while travelling on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The tube is London's Underground in the surface, but a Fallopian tube in the answer. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectopic pregnancy implants outside the womb, most often in a Fallopian tube.

clue.text: Not quite one to fancy nice explanations

definitions.text: Not quite one to fancy nice explanations

indicators.note: not quite the whole of the words, so only a run of letters straddling them is kept

blocks.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sceptic who is rather unwilling to accept a pleasant account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a wry description, while two of its words carry the letters across their join. 'Not quite' does double duty as the understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person believes people act from self-interest, so generous accounts of behaviour never persuade them.

clue.text: Setter's cooler with unknown Welsh girl

blocks.note: the setter speaking of what is theirs
a fan cools the air
W is the abbreviation for with
an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: The setter's cool drink is shared with a mysterious girl from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' gives MY as the setter speaks of something they own; x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Myfanwy is a traditional female first name in Wales, famous from a popular Welsh song.

clue.text: Soldier finds love in monster

indicators.note: in sets one piece inside the other

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a fire-breathing monster

explanation.surface: A fighter falls for a beast, like a knight smitten with the dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O as in a zero tennis score, slotted between the halves of the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was originally a mounted infantryman, and the name survives in cavalry regiments.

clue.text: Give instruction that is fractious, as formerly

blocks.note: to teach is to instruct
i.e., Latin id est

explanation.surface: A teacher's lesson is difficult because the pupil is being stroppy, in old-fashioned terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As formerly' flags an archaic word; it is the older form of tetchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachie is an obsolete spelling of tetchy, meaning irritable, peevish or touchy.

clue.text: Good heavens! One of those films! That's no way to do things!

definitions.text: That's no way to do things!

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of astonishment
a hint: the Carry On films were a long British comedy series

blocks.clueFragment: That's no way to do things!
blocks.note: second meaning: a protest at fuss or bad behaviour

explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were a long-running series of bawdy British comedies; a carry-on is also a fuss or commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses dismay at a commotion or disgraceful behaviour, the kind of protest someone shocked would make.
